Buy Your Next Home Cheap in Portage County, Ohio’s Tax Deed Sales

Portage County, Ohio, offers a great opportunity to acquire property for a fraction of its market value through its Tax Deed Sales. Sales occur on selected Mondays, and anyone of legal age can participate in owning real estate.

Understanding Tax Deed Sales

Tax Deed Sales in Portage County involve the sale of properties foreclosed due to unpaid property taxes. The county sells these properties to recover the owed taxes. Unlike tax lien sales, where you purchase the debt and earn interest, tax deed sales transfer the property’s ownership to the highest bidder.

How Does It Work?

When a property owner fails to pay their taxes, the Portage County Treasurer can initiate a foreclosure process through the Portage County Prosecutor. Entities like TaxEase Ohio LLC, F.I.G Taxes, or the Portage County Land Reutilization Corporation may seize properties.

  • Registration: Register with Real Auction, the official public sheriff’s sale website, where you will need to complete a Purchaser Information Form.
  • Bidding: Bidding starts at 11:00 AM on scheduled Mondays. Auctions are conducted individually online for each property.
  • Deposits: To participate, you need to deposit 10% of your intended bid amount. Tax Deed Sales in Portage County involve the sale of properties foreclosed due to unpaid property taxes.

Pro Tips for Portage County Tax Sale

  • Research Properties: Before bidding, research the properties available for sale. Look into their current condition, market value, and any potential liabilities.
  • Attend Webinars: Real Auction offers webinar training to help you understand the process. Contact Real Auction Customer Service at 1-877-361-7325 for more information.
  • Understand Legalities: To avoid legal complications, make sure you are familiar with Ohio’s tax sale laws and regulations.

Frequently Asked Questions for Portage County Auction

Q: What happens if property owners pay their taxes before the sale?

A: If the property owner pays the owed taxes before the sale, the auction will remove the property from the list.

Q: What are the costs associated with buying a property at a tax deed sale?

A: In addition to the bid amount, successful bidders must pay recorder’s fees, administrative/recording fees, auditor’s conveyance fees, and the sheriff’s deed fee.

Q: Can I inspect the properties before the sale?

A: Typically, properties sold at tax deed sales are not available for inspection prior to the auction. It’s essential to do as much research as possible using public records and other resources.
